headline: 82,500 fans to roar at MetLife Stadium for World Cup Final
summary: The legendary venue in New Jersey will host the 23rd FIFA World Cup final on July 19, marking the conclusion of the largest tournament in history.
details: The 23rd FIFA World Cup is the largest ever, featuring 48 teams for the first time. The tournament is being co-hosted by the USA, Canada, and Mexico.
The grand finale will take place at the world-famous MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The venue has already hosted seven matches in this tournament.
Spanning 2.1 million square feet, MetLife Stadium can accommodate 82,500 spectators, promising an electric atmosphere for the final match on July 19.
Beyond the World Cup, the stadium is renowned for hosting major events like the Copa América final, NFL matches, and WrestleMania.
It is also a premier destination for global superstars, having hosted concerts by Taylor Swift, BTS, Beyoncé, and Bruno Mars.
The stadium's name comes from a 25-year naming rights agreement signed in 2011 with MetLife, a global financial protection company.
MetLife has a presence in 24 of the 48 participating nations and has been operating in Bangladesh for over 74 years.

headline_marked: BNP's Fakhrul [[reaffirms commitment to July Charter]], accuses opposition of misleading public
headline: BNP's Fakhrul reaffirms commitment to July Charter, accuses opposition of misleading public
summary: LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir says the BNP remains committed to implementing every provision of the document, rejecting claims that they oppose it.
details: LGRD Minister and BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has accused the opposition of misleading the public over the July Charter, asserting that the BNP remains committed to implementing every provision of the document.
Speaking at a memorial meeting at the National Press Club in Dhaka, Fakhrul stated that all parties involved in the July 2024 movement signed the charter and the BNP will implement every word of it.
He rejected claims that the opposition would take the issue to the streets if the charter's demands were not met in parliament, calling such rhetoric 'misleading' and designed to sway public opinion.

Fakhrul clarified that the BNP had never agreed to proportional representation in the upper house, stating that the reform commission brought those proposals without their consent and that the nation had been deceived.
He emphasized that the July Charter should be implemented in line with the elected party's election manifesto, just as the BNP is committed to its own 31-point proposal.
The BNP leader also highlighted the BNP's history of introducing major reforms, such as the caretaker government system, to counter claims that they are against reform.
He alleged that opposition leaders are using the July Charter solely as a tool to gain power, rather than as a a genuine commitment to the movement's goals.
Fakhrul concluded by stating that the BNP secured a two-thirds majority based on its manifesto and that there should be no confusion regarding its position on constitutional amendments.
caption:
BNP's Mirza Fakhrul says the party is fully committed to the July Charter, but claims the opposition is using it to mislead the public.

LGRD Minister and BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has accused the opposition of misleading the public over the July Charter, asserting that the BNP remains committed to implementing every provision of the document.

Speaking at a memorial meeting at the National Press Club in Dhaka, Fakhrul stated that all parties involved in the July 2024 movement signed the charter and the BNP will implement every word of it.

He rejected claims that the opposition would take the issue to the streets if the charter's demands were not met in parliament, calling such rhetoric 'misleading' and designed to sway public opinion.

Fakhrul clarified that the BNP had never agreed to proportional representation in the upper house, stating that the reform commission brought those proposals without their consent and that the nation had been deceived.

He emphasized that the July Charter should be implemented in line with the elected party's election manifesto, just as the BNP is committed to its own 31-point proposal.

The BNP leader also highlighted the BNP's history of introducing major reforms, such as the caretaker government system, to counter claims that they are against reform.

He alleged that opposition leaders are using the July Charter solely as a tool to gain power, rather than as a a genuine commitment to the movement's goals.

Fakhrul concluded by stating that the BNP secured a two-thirds majority based on its manifesto and that there should be no confusion regarding its position on constitutional amendments.
